key_insight: An open-source toolkit turns RHEED from an operator-dependent diagnostic into an AI-accessible, automated control and analysis platform for thin-film growth.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to autonomous thin-film synthesis by enabling programmable RHEED alignment, quantitative analysis, and agent-driven experiment workflows on standard PLD hardware.
method: Programmable electron-optics control for RHEED instrumentation
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Shared GUI/API plus MCP server and adapter interface for AI analysis and RHEED simulation
evidence_signal: The toolkit is demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system, with an agent-driven example showing natural-language selection, configuration, and execution of quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Agentic workflows and extensible adapters will still depend on robust calibration, validation, and careful integration with diverse instruments and analysis methods.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
